guides.title: Why is my baby drinking less milk?
guides.metaTitle: Why is my baby drinking less milk?
guides.metaDescription: A sudden drop in bottles or feeds is usually distraction, a growth plateau, or teething — not a problem.

guides.title: Why won't my baby nap?
guides.metaTitle: Why won't my baby nap?
guides.metaDescription: Nine times out of ten it's the wake window — too short and they're not tired, too long and they're overtired.

guides.title: Is this sleep regression?
guides.metaTitle: Is this sleep regression?
guides.metaDescription: Probably. But 'regression' is a bad word for it — it's usually a permanent change in how your baby sleeps, or a new skill breaking through.

guides.title: How do I start solids without losing my mind?
guides.metaTitle: How do I start solids without losing my mind?
guides.metaDescription: Starting solids can be slow and messy; readiness, safe textures and gentle practice matter more than a perfect timetable.

guides.title: Why is my baby suddenly refusing the bottle?
guides.metaTitle: Why is my baby suddenly refusing the bottle?
guides.metaDescription: A sudden bottle refusal may be the flow, temperature, position, a sore mouth — or simply the bottle itself.

guides.title: Is my baby’s spit-up reflux or something else?
guides.metaTitle: Is my baby’s spit-up reflux or something else?
guides.metaDescription: A happy spitter is a laundry problem. A distressed one is worth a conversation with your doctor.

guides.title: Why is my baby waking at 5am?
guides.metaTitle: Why is my baby waking at 5am?
guides.metaDescription: Usually bedtime too late, nap timing, or light. Rarely a baby who's finished sleeping.

guides.title: Why is my newborn awake all night and asleep all day?
guides.metaTitle: Why is my newborn awake all night and asleep all day?
guides.metaDescription: Newborns have no body clock yet. You build it for them, with light and contrast.

guides.title: When will my baby roll, sit and crawl?
guides.metaTitle: When will my baby roll, sit and crawl?
guides.metaDescription: Ranges are wide and order varies. Some babies skip crawling entirely and are completely fine.

guides.title: When should my baby babble, point and say first words?
guides.metaTitle: When should my baby babble, point and say first words?
guides.metaDescription: Understanding comes long before speaking, and gestures matter more than word count.

guides.title: Is teething making my baby miserable?
guides.metaTitle: Is teething making my baby miserable?
guides.metaDescription: Teething causes drool, gnawing and grumpiness. It does not cause high fever, diarrhoea or rashes elsewhere.

guides.title: What should I know about my baby’s first fever?
guides.metaTitle: What should I know about my baby’s first fever?
guides.metaDescription: The number matters far less than the age of your baby and how they look between temperature spikes.

guides.title: Why won’t my baby’s nappy rash clear up?
guides.metaTitle: Why won’t my baby’s nappy rash clear up?
guides.metaDescription: Simple nappy rash often improves with gentle cleaning, dry skin and barrier cream; spreading or persistent rash needs another look.

guides.title: Is it normal to feel like I can’t handle one more person touching me?
guides.metaTitle: Is it normal to feel like I can’t handle one more person…
guides.metaDescription: Wanting your body back for twenty minutes doesn't make you a bad parent. It makes you a mammal.

guides.title: How do we split the nights so nobody breaks?
guides.metaTitle: How do we split the nights so nobody breaks?
guides.metaDescription: Both of you half-sleeping is worse than one of you sleeping properly. Shifts beat solidarity.

guides.title: How do we manage visitors after the baby arrives?
guides.metaTitle: How do we manage visitors after the baby arrives?
guides.metaDescription: Decide the rules before you're standing in the doorway holding a baby and a wet muslin.

guides.title: Where should my newborn sleep?
guides.metaTitle: Where should my newborn sleep?
guides.metaDescription: The safest place for a newborn to sleep is on their back, on a firm, flat and completely clear sleep surface.

guides.title: Are newborn hiccups normal?
guides.metaTitle: Are newborn hiccups normal?
guides.metaDescription: Newborn hiccups are very common, usually bother parents more than babies and do not normally stop a comfortable baby from sleeping.

guides.title: How do you unblock a newborn's nose?
guides.metaTitle: How do you unblock a newborn's nose?
guides.metaDescription: Saline, humidity and patience can help a blocked newborn nose, but turning your baby upside down is not the answer, even at 2am.

guides.title: Why is my newborn so noisy while sleeping?
guides.metaTitle: Why is my newborn so noisy while sleeping?
guides.metaDescription: Grunting, squeaking, kicking and arm-waving can all happen during normal newborn sleep, even when your baby is deeply asleep.

guides.title: Why did milk come out of my baby's nose?
guides.metaTitle: Why did milk come out of my baby's nose?
guides.metaDescription: Milk can sometimes come through a baby’s nose during spit-up because the mouth and nose connect at the back of the throat.

guides.title: Why did my baby spit up hours after a feed?
guides.metaTitle: Why did my baby spit up hours after a feed?
guides.metaDescription: Small spit-ups can happen hours after a feed, while repeated forceful vomiting is the version worth getting checked.

guides.title: Why does my newborn breathe fast and then slow down?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my newborn breathe fast and then slow down?
guides.metaDescription: Newborn breathing can switch between faster and slower bursts, but breathing effort and colour matter more than speed alone.

guides.title: Why did my newborn's body shake for a second?
guides.metaTitle: Why did my newborn's body shake for a second?
guides.metaDescription: Newborns often startle, tremble or twitch, but repeated movement or reduced awareness is worth getting checked.

guides.title: Why does my baby sleep with their mouth open?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby sleep with their mouth open?
guides.metaDescription: Sleeping with an open mouth can be harmless, but persistent mouth breathing is worth checking alongside feeding and breathing effort.

guides.title: Should I wake my baby to change a wet nappy?
guides.metaTitle: Should I wake my baby to change a wet nappy?
guides.metaDescription: Poo gets changed quickly. A wet nappy can usually wait until she's up anyway. Modern nappies are better at this than your anxiety suggests.

guides.title: Why does my newborn want milk again so soon?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my newborn want milk again so soon?
guides.metaDescription: Responsive feeding follows your baby’s cues, but a feeding plan given for a medical reason always comes first.

guides.title: Do I time the next feed from the start or end of the last one?
guides.metaTitle: Do I time the next feed from the start or end of the last one?
guides.metaDescription: Feeding intervals are usually counted from the start of one feed to the start of the next, unless your baby has a different plan.

guides.title: Is it normal for a newborn to lose weight after birth?
guides.metaTitle: Is it normal for a newborn to lose weight after birth?
guides.metaDescription: Some newborn weight loss is expected in the first days, and the turning point matters more than one number on the scale.

guides.title: Do newborn babies blink less than adults?
guides.metaTitle: Do newborn babies blink less than adults?
guides.metaDescription: Newborns blink far less than adults, so a long unbroken stare can be completely ordinary.

guides.title: Was that a real baby smile or just wind?
guides.metaTitle: Was that a real baby smile or just wind?
guides.metaDescription: Early baby smiles are usually spontaneous rather than social, but you are still allowed to take them personally.

guides.title: When does the milk actually come in?
guides.metaTitle: When does the milk actually come in?
guides.metaDescription: Thick, yellow colostrum is expected at first; fuller milk volume often arrives between days two and five and can be later after a caesarean.

guides.title: How often should I pump around the clock?
guides.metaTitle: How often should I pump around the clock?
guides.metaDescription: Roughly eight sessions in twenty-four hours, and one longer gap at night that you plan for rather than fall into.

guides.title: Why has my milk supply dropped on one side?
guides.metaTitle: Why has my milk supply dropped on one side?
guides.metaDescription: Sides are rarely equal, and supply follows demand. The most common answer is the least satisfying one: missed sessions.

guides.title: Is this a blocked milk duct or mastitis?
guides.metaTitle: Is this a blocked milk duct or mastitis?
guides.metaDescription: A tender lump usually clears with milk moving through it. Heat, redness or feeling unwell changes the answer and shouldn't wait.

guides.title: How long can expressed milk sit out?
guides.metaTitle: How long can expressed milk sit out?
guides.metaDescription: Room temperature buys you a few hours, and a warm room buys you fewer. If your baby is in hospital, their rules override every chart online.

guides.title: How do I keep expressed milk ready when we are out?
guides.metaTitle: How do I keep expressed milk ready when we are out?
guides.metaDescription: Carry it cold and warm it when you need it. Holding milk at feeding temperature for hours is the thing to avoid.

guides.title: What do the different NICU stages mean?
guides.metaTitle: What do the different NICU stages mean?
guides.metaDescription: The numbers describe how much support your baby needs, not how she's doing overall. And they don't only go one way.

guides.title: Why does the incubator show such a low temperature?
guides.metaTitle: Why does the incubator show such a low temperature?
guides.metaDescription: A NICU screen may show the incubator setting rather than your baby’s temperature, so ask what the number is measuring before interpreting it.

guides.title: Is there a minimum weight before she can come home?
guides.metaTitle: Is there a minimum weight before she can come home?
guides.metaDescription: Almost everyone asks about the number. Readiness is really about three things she has to be doing herself, and weight is not one of them.

guides.title: Why can my premature baby only manage a little milk?
guides.metaTitle: Why can my premature baby only manage a little milk?
guides.metaDescription: Not appetite — stamina. Sucking, swallowing and breathing in sequence is genuinely hard work, and it comes with time rather than encouragement.

guides.title: Why is my premature baby’s tummy firm and bloated?
guides.metaTitle: Why is my premature baby’s tummy firm and bloated?
guides.metaDescription: A swollen, firm abdomen in a small baby is one to raise straight away rather than watch. In hospital it is taken seriously fast, and there are good…

guides.title: What is corrected age and when should I use it?
guides.metaTitle: What is corrected age and when should I use it?
guides.metaDescription: Count from the due date, not the birthday. It's a small arithmetic change that removes an enormous amount of unnecessary worry.

guides.title: Which growth chart should a premature baby use?
guides.metaTitle: Which growth chart should a premature baby use?
guides.metaDescription: Percentiles are close to meaningless for a baby born early unless you're using the right chart and the right age. Her own trend is the number that matters.

guides.title: When can I take my newborn out?
guides.metaTitle: When can I take my newborn out?
guides.metaDescription: The forty days thing is custom more than medicine. The real answer depends on her, and for a baby born early it depends more.

guides.title: Is it normal not to feel an instant bond with my baby?
guides.metaTitle: Is it normal not to feel an instant bond with my baby?
guides.metaDescription: Common, rarely said out loud, and not a verdict on the kind of father you'll be. It usually arrives later and through doing rather than feeling.

guides.title: What colour should my baby’s poo be?
guides.metaTitle: What colour should my baby’s poo be?
guides.metaDescription: A simple guide to normal newborn poo colours, what changes with feeding, and the three colours worth calling about.

guides.title: How long can a baby go without pooing?
guides.metaTitle: How long can a baby go without pooing?
guides.metaDescription: Babies can have surprisingly long gaps between poos; softness, feeding and wet nappies matter more than the clock alone.

guides.title: Why does my baby cry every evening?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby cry every evening?
guides.metaDescription: Predictable evening crying is common and exhausting; movement, less stimulation and swapping parents can make it more manageable.

guides.title: Why does my baby have so much wind?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby have so much wind?
guides.metaDescription: Swallowed air and an immature gut make wind common; pacing, winding and gentle movement helped us more than rushing feeds.

guides.title: Do colic drops actually help?
guides.metaTitle: Do colic drops actually help?
guides.metaDescription: Infacol and probiotic drops help some babies modestly; try one thing at a time and avoid homemade additions to a young baby’s milk.

guides.title: What are the little bumps on my newborn’s face?
guides.metaTitle: What are the little bumps on my newborn’s face?
guides.metaDescription: Milia and newborn acne are common and usually clear alone; fever, blisters or a non-fading rash need medical advice.

guides.title: How can I tell if my newborn is actually in pain?
guides.metaTitle: How can I tell if my newborn is actually in pain?
guides.metaDescription: Newborns groan, fidget and clear their throats in normal sleep; colour, breathing and a genuinely different cry tell you more than noise alone.

guides.title: How long should I sterilise baby bottles?
guides.metaTitle: How long should I sterilise baby bottles?
guides.metaDescription: Wash feeding equipment thoroughly and sterilise it for the first year under UK guidance; premature babies may need stricter instructions.

guides.title: Is my baby too hot, and is air conditioning safe?
guides.metaTitle: Is my baby too hot, and is air conditioning safe?
guides.metaDescription: Check your baby’s chest or neck rather than cool hands; air conditioning is useful when the room stays comfortable and airflow is not direct.

guides.title: When will my baby hold their head up?
guides.metaTitle: When will my baby hold their head up?
guides.metaDescription: Head control builds gradually through short tummy-time practice; use corrected age after premature birth and keep supporting the head until control is…

guides.title: Will sleeping with the head to one side cause a flat head?
guides.metaTitle: Will sleeping with the head to one side cause a flat head?
guides.metaDescription: Flat spots are common and often improve as babies move more; vary awake positioning but never change safe back sleeping to fix head shape.

guides.title: Should I swaddle my baby or let them kick?
guides.metaTitle: Should I swaddle my baby or let them kick?
guides.metaDescription: Swaddling may settle a newborn while free awake movement builds strength; keep hips loose and stop at the first signs of rolling.

guides.title: How long do vaccine side effects last in babies?
guides.metaTitle: How long do vaccine side effects last in babies?
guides.metaDescription: A day or two of irritability, sleepiness or reduced appetite can be expected; persistent vomiting, dehydration or unusual sleepiness needs advice.

guides.title: Is my baby’s big round tummy normal?
guides.metaTitle: Is my baby’s big round tummy normal?
guides.metaDescription: A soft round tummy after feeding is usually normal baby shape; a firm shiny tummy with pain or vomiting needs checking.

guides.title: Is it normal to regret having a baby sometimes?
guides.metaTitle: Is it normal to regret having a baby sometimes?
guides.metaDescription: Overload can produce frightening thoughts without making them true; saying it early and protecting real sleep can stop shame making everything heavier.

guides.title: How much milk should my baby have?
guides.metaTitle: How much milk should my baby have?
guides.metaDescription: A practical guide to how much milk babies may need, why feeds vary and why nappies and growth matter more than one unfinished bottle.

guides.title: How can I tell how much milk my breastfed baby is getting?
guides.metaTitle: How can I tell how much milk my breastfed baby is getting?
guides.metaDescription: You cannot measure a breastfeed directly, but swallowing, wet nappies and steady growth can show whether your baby is getting enough milk.

guides.title: Why does my baby always seem hungry?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby always seem hungry?
guides.metaDescription: Frequent feeding can mean growth, comfort, tiredness or trapped air rather than underfeeding; nappies and growth tell the clearer story.

guides.title: Why does my baby drink too fast and then vomit?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby drink too fast and then vomit?
guides.metaDescription: Paced bottle feeding can slow a fast drinker, reduce swallowed air and help your baby notice when she has had enough.

guides.title: What is cluster feeding?
guides.metaTitle: What is cluster feeding?
guides.metaDescription: Cluster feeding means several feeds close together, often in the evening, and does not automatically mean your milk supply is low.

guides.title: Why does my baby get sleepy during feeds?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby get sleepy during feeds?
guides.metaDescription: Babies often become sleepier after a growth spurt, but being unusually hard to wake or taking much less milk needs checking.

guides.title: Is my baby gaining enough weight?
guides.metaTitle: Is my baby gaining enough weight?
guides.metaDescription: Daily weights jump around; growth over time, wet nappies and how your baby feeds give a more useful picture.

guides.title: Which baby formula is best?
guides.metaTitle: Which baby formula is best?
guides.metaDescription: Standard first infant formulas are nutritionally complete; availability, preparation and your baby’s medical needs matter more than price.

guides.title: How do I move from breast milk to formula?
guides.metaTitle: How do I move from breast milk to formula?
guides.metaDescription: A gradual move from breast milk to formula can be easier on your baby’s tummy and kinder to your own milk supply.

guides.title: Does breastfeeding for three months still count?
guides.metaTitle: Does breastfeeding for three months still count?
guides.metaDescription: Breastfeeding for three months still matters; there is no cliff edge where the time and effort suddenly stop counting.

guides.title: How do I stop pumping without it hurting?
guides.metaTitle: How do I stop pumping without it hurting?
guides.metaDescription: Reduce pumping gradually, dropping one session at a time, so your body can adjust without painful fullness or blocked ducts.

guides.title: How do I make up a formula bottle safely?
guides.metaTitle: How do I make up a formula bottle safely?
guides.metaDescription: Use freshly boiled water and let it cool to reduce bacteria in formula powder, follow the tin exactly and make feeds fresh whenever possible.

guides.title: Is it normal for my baby not to poo after switching to formula?
guides.metaTitle: Is it normal for my baby not to poo after switching to formula?
guides.metaDescription: Longer gaps and firmer poo can happen after switching to formula; a soft tummy and a comfortable baby are reassuring signs.

guides.title: What changes when my baby starts formula?
guides.metaTitle: What changes when my baby starts formula?
guides.metaDescription: Formula can change nappies, gas and feeding gaps while your baby adjusts; allergy signs and repeated vomiting need separate advice.

guides.title: Why was my baby’s vomit yellow?
guides.metaTitle: Why was my baby’s vomit yellow?
guides.metaDescription: Curdled milk can look creamy or pale yellow, but true yellow, yellow-green or green vomit in a baby needs urgent medical advice.

guides.title: How much should my baby be sleeping?
guides.metaTitle: How much should my baby be sleeping?
guides.metaDescription: Newborns often sleep for fourteen to seventeen hours in short stretches; feeding, wet nappies and alertness matter more than one exact total.

guides.title: Why won't my baby sleep? Is she just not tired?
guides.metaTitle: Why won't my baby sleep? Is she just not tired?
guides.metaDescription: A baby who fights sleep may be overtired rather than wide awake; learn the early signs and what can make settling easier.

guides.title: Could my baby's nappy be stopping her from settling?
guides.metaTitle: Could my baby's nappy be stopping her from settling?
guides.metaDescription: A wet, tight or uncomfortable nappy can keep a tired baby awake; this simple checklist helps you rule out the physical things first.

guides.title: How can I put my sleeping baby down without waking her?
guides.metaTitle: How can I put my sleeping baby down without waking her?
guides.metaDescription: Waiting for deeper sleep and lowering your baby gently can make cot transfers easier without starting the whole settling routine again.

guides.title: Why does my baby suddenly open her eyes while sleeping?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby suddenly open her eyes while sleeping?
guides.metaDescription: The startle reflex and normal sleep cycles can make a baby suddenly open her eyes; learn what usually helps and when to ask for advice.

guides.title: My baby slept for six hours. Should I have woken her?
guides.metaTitle: My baby slept for six hours. Should I have woken her?
guides.metaDescription: A six-hour sleep can be fine once a baby is feeding and growing well, but babies on a feeding plan may still need to be woken.

guides.title: Why does my baby nap briefly but sleep for hours at night?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby nap briefly but sleep for hours at night?
guides.metaDescription: Short daytime naps and longer night stretches can be normal because night sleep often settles before daytime sleep does.

guides.title: Why does my baby sleep through every noise?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby sleep through every noise?
guides.metaDescription: Many newborns sleep through noise at first; learn why that changes and how steady background sound may help later.

guides.title: My baby won't wake up. When should I worry?
guides.metaTitle: My baby won't wake up. When should I worry?
guides.metaDescription: Long sleep can be normal, but a baby who is hard to wake, floppy, pale or missing feeds needs urgent medical advice.

guides.title: When will my baby sleep through the night?
guides.metaTitle: When will my baby sleep through the night?
guides.metaDescription: Sleeping through the night usually develops slowly, and often means five or six hours rather than a full ten-hour night.

guides.title: For a premature baby, does sleep or feeding matter more?
guides.metaTitle: For a premature baby, does sleep or feeding matter more?
guides.metaDescription: Premature babies may tire quickly while feeding, so early feeding plans and corrected age matter more than general sleep advice.

guides.title: Does my baby need a sleep schedule?
guides.metaTitle: Does my baby need a sleep schedule?
guides.metaDescription: A flexible routine can help without forcing a strict clock; keep the order familiar and let the times change as your baby grows.

guides.title: Is it okay to take my baby for a walk at night?
guides.metaTitle: Is it okay to take my baby for a walk at night?
guides.metaDescription: A night walk can help a baby settle when the pram stays uncovered, she is dressed safely and she moves to a flat sleep surface at home.

guides.title: What does months of broken sleep do to parents?
guides.metaTitle: What does months of broken sleep do to parents?
guides.metaDescription: Broken sleep can affect mood, patience and judgement; protected blocks of sleep and asking for help can make a real difference.

guides.title: My baby has slept most of today. Is that okay?
guides.metaTitle: My baby has slept most of today. Is that okay?
guides.metaDescription: A sleepy day can be normal during a growth spurt, but sleepiness with poor feeding or difficulty waking needs medical advice.

guides.title: Why does my baby keep putting her hands in her mouth?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby keep putting her hands in her mouth?
guides.metaDescription: Hands in the mouth and fingers meeting in the middle are early signs that your baby is discovering her body, not always signs of hunger.

guides.title: Why don't my baby's eyes move together yet?
guides.metaTitle: Why don't my baby's eyes move together yet?
guides.metaDescription: Occasional eye crossing can be common in young babies, but a constant turn or white reflection in the pupil needs medical advice.

guides.title: Is camera flash safe for my baby's eyes?
guides.metaTitle: Is camera flash safe for my baby's eyes?
guides.metaDescription: An ordinary camera flash is unlikely to harm a baby's eyes; learn what to avoid and why a white reflection in photos should be checked.

guides.title: When should I start playing with my newborn?
guides.metaTitle: When should I start playing with my newborn?
guides.metaDescription: Newborn play is simple and brief: faces, talking, cuddles and short tummy-time sessions are already enough stimulation.

guides.title: How long should I wait after a feed before tummy time?
guides.metaTitle: How long should I wait after a feed before tummy time?
guides.metaDescription: Tummy time is usually more comfortable before a feed or after allowing time for milk to settle, especially for babies who spit up.

guides.title: Why does my baby's head control seem worse?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby's head control seem worse?
guides.metaDescription: Head control can look uneven while a baby is learning, but a lasting tilt, stiffness or reduced movement should be checked.

guides.title: When do babies start laughing?
guides.metaTitle: When do babies start laughing?
guides.metaDescription: Most babies begin laughing in the early months, often at an unexpected sound, face or toy rather than anything carefully planned.

guides.title: When do babies start talking?
guides.metaTitle: When do babies start talking?
guides.metaDescription: Talking develops through coos, babbling, gestures and understanding before first words arrive; corrected age matters for premature babies.

guides.title: Why does my baby roll one way but not the other?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby roll one way but not the other?
guides.metaDescription: Babies often learn to roll in one direction before the other; once rolling begins, sleep and changing safety need to change too.

guides.title: Do I need to teach my baby to sit?
guides.metaTitle: Do I need to teach my baby to sit?
guides.metaDescription: Babies usually learn to sit through floor play and practice rather than formal training; steady support and time do most of the work.

guides.title: Why does my baby favour one hand?
guides.metaTitle: Why does my baby favour one hand?
guides.metaDescription: A small preference can happen, but consistently avoiding one hand or one side before eighteen months is worth discussing with a professional.

guides.title: What can I do with my three-month-old?
guides.metaTitle: What can I do with my three-month-old?
guides.metaDescription: Simple, repeated play is enough for a three-month-old: talking, faces, floor time, reaching and stopping when she has had enough.

guides.title: Which baby toys are actually worth buying?
guides.metaTitle: Which baby toys are actually worth buying?
guides.metaDescription: The most useful baby toys are simple, safe and suited to the stage; you do not need a room full of expensive equipment.

guides.title: When will my baby play independently?
guides.metaTitle: When will my baby play independently?
guides.metaDescription: Independent play starts in very short bursts and grows slowly; staying nearby and making the space safe can help it develop.

guides.title: Why am I caring for my baby but not enjoying it?
guides.metaTitle: Why am I caring for my baby but not enjoying it?
guides.metaDescription: Going through the motions can be a sign of exhaustion rather than a lack of love; practical help and honest support matter.

guides.title: What should I do when my baby has her first cold?
guides.metaTitle: What should I do when my baby has her first cold?
